definitions.explanation: An approximate number of people, typically implying somewhere between two or three and about ten. A common way to express a small, indefinite number of people.

examples.japanese: {数人|すうにん}の{友達|ともだち}と{会|あ}った。
examples.english: I met with a few friends.

examples.japanese: {教室|きょうしつ}に{数人|すうにん}の{生徒|せいと}が{残|のこ}っていた。
examples.english: Several students were still in the classroom.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}{現場|げんば}には{数人|すうにん}の{目撃者|もくげきしゃ}がいたが、{証言|しょうげん}はそれぞれ{異|こと}なっていた。
examples.english: There were several eyewitnesses at the accident scene, but their testimonies differed.

notes: The prefix {数|すう}～ means "several" or "a few" and combines with many counters: {数回|すうかい} (several times), {数日|すうじつ} (several days), {数年|すうねん} (several years), {数百|すうひゃく} (several hundred). The range implied by {数|すう}～ is roughly 2–9, though context determines the perceived quantity. Related: {何人|なんにん}か (some number of people — similar but phrased as a question-based indefinite), {数名|すうめい} (several people — more formal variant using {名|めい}).
